\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆ} (ḍikki hoḍe)}{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ ಹೊಡೆ (ḍikki hoḍe)}]{\kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆ} (ḍikki hoḍe) — to collide; to crash into}

\label{lesson:KA-C330-dikki-hode}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to announce, then the Kannada for a statement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆ}} — \emph{ḍikki hoḍe} — \textquotedblleft{}to collide; to crash into\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಕಾರು} \kn{ಬಸ್ಸಿಗೆ} \kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆಯಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ondu kāru bassige ḍikki hoḍeyitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A car crashed into a bus.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆದೆ}, \emph{ḍikki hoḍede}.

What is hit takes -\kn{ಗೆ}: \kn{ಮರಕ್ಕೆ} \kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆ}, to crash into a tree.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆ}} (\emph{ḍikki hoḍe}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 443 lists Kannada \emph{ḍikki}, \textquotedblleft{}a butt, a collision\textquotedblright{}, with words for hitting against, and \emph{hoḍe} is \textquotedblleft{}to strike, to beat\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4252).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍikki hoḍe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍikki hoḍe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ondu kāru bassige ḍikki hoḍeyitu.} — A car crashed into a bus.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to announce, then the Kannada for a statement, then say \emph{ḍikki hoḍe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಡಿಕ್ಕಿ} \kn{ಹೊಡೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To collide; to crash into\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿ} (pratyakṣadarśi)}{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿ (pratyakṣadarśi)}]{\kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿ} (pratyakṣadarśi) — an eyewitness}

\label{lesson:KA-C330-pratyaksadarsi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a statement, then the Kannada for to collide.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿ}} — \emph{pratyakṣadarśi} — \textquotedblleft{}an eyewitness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಒಬ್ಬ} \kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿ} \kn{ಪೊಲೀಸರಿಗೆ} \kn{ಎಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ} \kn{ಹೇಳಿದನು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{obba pratyakṣadarśi polīsarige ellavannū hēḷidanu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
An eyewitness told the police everything.
\end{quote}

Plural: \kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿಗಳು}, \emph{pratyakṣadarśigaḷu}.

\kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷ}, before the eyes, and \kn{ದರ್ಶಿ}, one who sees.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿ}} (\emph{pratyakṣadarśi}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{pratyakṣadarśin}, \textquotedblleft{}seeing a thing with one's own eyes\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratyakṣadarśi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratyakṣadarśi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{obba pratyakṣadarśi polīsarige ellavannū hēḷidanu.} — An eyewitness told the police everything.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a statement, then the Kannada for to collide, then say \emph{pratyakṣadarśi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷದರ್ಶಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An eyewitness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಹಾನಿ} (hāni)}{ಹಾನಿ (hāni)}]{\kn{ಹಾನಿ} (hāni) — damage; harm}

\label{lesson:KA-C330-hani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to collide, then the Kannada for an eyewitness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಹಾನಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಹಾನಿ}} — \emph{hāni} — \textquotedblleft{}damage; harm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಅಪಘಾತದಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಕಾರಿಗೆ} \kn{ತುಂಬಾ} \kn{ಹಾನಿ} \kn{ಆಯಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{apaghātadalli kārige tumbā hāni āyitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The car was badly damaged in the accident.
\end{quote}

What is damaged takes -\kn{ಗೆ}: \kn{ಕಾರಿಗೆ} \kn{ಹಾನಿ} \kn{ಆಯಿತು}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಹಾನಿ}} (\emph{hāni}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{hāni}, \textquotedblleft{}abandonment, loss, decrease\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hāni}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hāni}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{apaghātadalli kārige tumbā hāni āyitu.} — The car was badly damaged in the accident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to collide, then the Kannada for an eyewitness, then say \emph{hāni} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಹಾನಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Damage; harm\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಮೃತ} (mṛta)}{ಮೃತ (mṛta)}]{\kn{ಮೃತ} (mṛta) — the deceased; dead}

\label{lesson:KA-C330-mrta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for an eyewitness, then the Kannada for damage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಮೃತ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಮೃತ}} — \emph{mṛta} — \textquotedblleft{}the deceased; dead\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಅಪಘಾತದಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಮೃತರಾದವರ} \kn{ಹೆಸರುಗಳು} \kn{ಪತ್ರಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಬಂದವು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{apaghātadalli mṛtarādavara hesarugaḷu patrikeyalli bandavu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The names of those who died in the accident came out in the paper.
\end{quote}

A news word: \kn{ಮೃತರಾದರು}, they died; \kn{ಮೃತರ} \kn{ಕುಟುಂಬ}, the family of the dead.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಮೃತ}} (\emph{mṛta}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{mṛta}, \textquotedblleft{}dead, deceased\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), from the root \emph{mṛ}, \textquotedblleft{}to die\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mṛta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mṛta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{apaghātadalli mṛtarādavara hesarugaḷu patrikeyalli bandavu.} — The names of those who died in the accident came out in the paper.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for an eyewitness, then the Kannada for damage, then say \emph{mṛta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಮೃತ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The deceased; dead\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಅವಘಡ} (avaghaḍa)}{ಅವಘಡ (avaghaḍa)}]{\kn{ಅವಘಡ} (avaghaḍa) — a mishap}

\label{lesson:KA-C330-avaghada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for damage, then the Kannada for the deceased.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಅವಘಡ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಅವಘಡ}} — \emph{avaghaḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}a mishap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಸಣ್ಣ} \kn{ಅವಘಡ} \kn{ಆಯಿತು}, \kn{ಯಾರಿಗೂ} \kn{ಏನೂ} \kn{ಆಗಲಿಲ್ಲ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kārkhāneyalli saṇṇa avaghaḍa āyitu, yārigū ēnū āgalilla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a small mishap at the factory; nobody was hurt.
\end{quote}

A news word for an accident with fire, gas or machines.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಅವಘಡ}} (\emph{avaghaḍa}) is a Kannada word of the newspapers whose origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaghaḍa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaghaḍa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kārkhāneyalli saṇṇa avaghaḍa āyitu, yārigū ēnū āgalilla.} — There was a small mishap at the factory; nobody was hurt.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for damage, then the Kannada for the deceased, then say \emph{avaghaḍa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಅವಘಡ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A mishap\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
